sources: catalog/php/releases.json (variant/arch/kind fields, scraped from windows.php.net and php.net/releases)
catalog/php/gaps.json (Windows x86/x64 and Linux/macOS binary gaps, with reasons)
catalog/php/NOTES.md (this catalog's own research notes on sources and mirror coverage)

milestones.notes: namespaces (PEP-style single-level, backslash-separated) added in 5.3.0; no autoloading standard until PSR-0/PSR-4 (Composer era)
PHP has never had generics; static analysis tools (PHPStan, Psalm) fake them via PHPDoc

no async/await keyword; Fibers (8.1) give cooperative primitives that ReactPHP/Amp build event loops and coroutine-style APIs on top of; before 8.1 those libraries relied on generators (5.5) and callbacks
no native threads in mainstream builds; ext-parallel and pthreads require a ZTS (thread-safe) build and are rarely available prebuilt; Swoole/Fibers give concurrency without OS threads
single-threaded execution model throughout; parallelism in practice means multiple processes (php-fpm workers, pcntl_fork on Unix only) or the ext-parallel/pthreads extensions on ZTS builds

STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLS_CLIENT negotiated up to TLS 1.2 in 5.6.0-5.6.6, then a fix reverted default negotiation to TLS 1.0-only for 5.6.7 through 7.1.x; TLS 1.2 became the reliable default again in 7.2.0 (rfc:improved-tls-defaults). Actual availability also depends on the OpenSSL the build was linked against
available only when compiled/linked against OpenSSL 1.1.1+; official Windows builds began bundling an OpenSSL 1.1.1 line around 7.4, Linux distro packages depend on the distro's OpenSSL

ext-curl exposes whatever the linked libcurl supports; CURL_HTTP_VERSION_2_0 usable once PHP is linked against an nghttp2-enabled libcurl (Windows builds bundled a suitable libcurl from roughly 5.5/5.6 on); no capability without the curl extension
no official ext-curl/libcurl build in this catalog exposes HTTP/3; requires a libcurl built with an HTTP/3 backend (quiche/ngtcp2), which php.net/windows.php.net do not ship
Composer (2012) is the de facto package manager but is never bundled with the PHP runtime itself; PEAR shipped with older builds but predates and is unrelated to Composer-era workflows

first Windows x64 archives appear on windows.php.net for the 5.5 line (catalog gaps.json: 'windows.php.net never shipped an x64 build for this branch (64-bit Windows PHP builds only began with the PHP 5.5 line)' for 5.4 and earlier); 5.5/5.6 x64 builds still used a 32-bit PHP integer/long internally, so true 64-bit PHP_INT_MAX on Windows only arrived with the 7.0 engine rewrite
no official ARM64 Windows build exists in any major covered here; windows.php.net ships x86/x64 only
php.net ships no macOS binaries at all (any arch); Apple Silicon support comes only from third parties (Homebrew, static-php-cli, distro-style packagers), not from php.net
php.net ships no Linux binaries at all (any arch); arm64 Linux PHP comes from distro packages or static-php-cli, not php.net

PHP strings remain byte arrays with no native Unicode string type in any released major (the PHP 6 Unicode-string project was abandoned before release); mbstring/intl provide Unicode-aware functions as an opt-in layer

os_support.windows: Windows 98/NT4/2000/XP/2003 era; x86 only, VC6-built binaries, no x64 build ever existed for this branch
os_support.macos: no official php.net binary; ran via source compile or OS-bundled PHP (Mac OS X shipped PHP 4 in /usr/bin from 10.2 onward)
os_support.linux: no official php.net binary; source tarball only, packaged by distros

added: Zend Engine 1 with reference-counted, largely value-semantic objects
limitations: objects behave like values (copied on assignment) rather than references, making OOP code fragile (fixed by Zend Engine 2 object handles in PHP 5.0)
no exceptions before 5.0 (try/catch does not exist)
no namespaces (5.3), no closures (5.3)
no SPL, no PDO
no built-in opcode cache (bundled OPcache is 5.5); relied on third-party APC/Zend Optimizer
long since end-of-life; no TLS 1.2/1.3 concerns apply because it predates modern OpenSSL stream wrapper defaults entirely and using it on the internet today is a security liability regardless

os_support.windows: Windows 98/NT4/2000/XP/2003; x86 only, VC6-built, no x64 build
os_support.macos: no official php.net binary; source compile only
os_support.linux: no official php.net binary; source tarball only

added: Zend Engine 2: objects now handled by reference/handle, not copied by value
limitations: no namespaces (5.3) -- large codebases used prefix-based faux-namespacing (Zend_Db, PEAR_...)
no closures/anonymous functions (5.3); callbacks used string/array callables
no late static binding (5.3), so 'self::' inside inherited static methods could not be overridden politely
no built-in unit testing, no Composer (2012) -- dependencies were vendored by hand or via PEAR
no bundled opcode cache
very early and buggy; many production sites skipped straight to 5.1/5.2

os_support.windows: Windows 98/NT4/2000/XP/2003; x86 only, VC6-built, no x64 build
os_support.macos: no official php.net binary; source compile only
os_support.linux: no official php.net binary; source tarball only

added: much improved performance and stability over 5.0
limitations: no namespaces, closures, or late static binding (all land in 5.3)
no Composer-era autoloading standard; spl_autoload_register appears in 5.1.2 but PSR-4 conventions came years later
no bundled opcode cache

os_support.windows: Windows 2000/XP/2003/Vista; x86 only, VC6-built, no x64 build
os_support.macos: no official php.net binary; source compile only
os_support.linux: no official php.net binary; source tarball only

limitations: no namespaces, closures, or late static binding (5.3)
no Composer (2012); PEAR was the standard package channel
no bundled opcode cache; APC was the common third-party choice
last major before the long-lived 5.3 line; widely used but security-EOL since 2011

os_support.windows: Windows XP SP3/2003 and later; x86 only (no x64 build), VC9-built (Visual Studio 2008)
os_support.macos: no official php.net binary; source compile only
os_support.linux: no official php.net binary; source tarball only

added: closures / anonymous functions (Closure class, 'use' clause for captured variables)
Zend Optimizer+ predecessor NOT yet bundled (that is 5.5)
limitations: no generators/yield (5.5)
no bundled opcode cache -- still relied on APC or commercial Zend Optimizer+
no scalar type hints or return types (7.0)
closures could not be bound to arbitrary objects until Closure::bind/bindTo landed in 5.4
no traits (5.4)
Composer (published 2012) targets 5.3.2+ as its practical floor, so 5.3.0/5.3.1 predate the ecosystem that made namespaces useful for autoloading

os_support.windows: Windows XP SP3/2003 and later; x86 only (no x64 build for this branch), VC9-built
os_support.macos: no official php.net binary; source compile only
os_support.linux: no official php.net binary; source tarball only

added: array dereferencing on function calls foo()[0]
limitations: no generators (5.5)
no bundled opcode cache (5.5)
no 64-bit Windows build at all -- large in-process arrays/strings were constrained to a 32-bit address space on Windows
no scalar/return type declarations (7.0)

os_support.windows: Windows Vista/Server 2008 and later (Windows XP/Server 2003 support dropped -- first line requiring VC11/Visual Studio 2012 runtime); first line with an official x64 build, alongside x86
os_support.macos: no official php.net binary; source compile only
os_support.linux: no official php.net binary; source tarball only

added: OPcache bundled with core for the first time (as the Zend Optimizer+ donation), though disabled by default
limitations: OPcache ships but is opt-in (opcache.enable=0 by default) -- enabled-by-default arrives with 7.0
the new x64 Windows build still used a 32-bit internal integer type, so PHP_INT_MAX on Windows x64 was the same as on x86 until PHP 7's engine rewrite
no scalar/return type declarations (7.0)

no Fibers/coroutine primitives -- async libraries of the era (ReactPHP, launched 2012) relied purely on callback-based event loops, not generators-as-coroutines patterns, until this release made generator-based coroutines practical

os_support.windows: Windows Vista/Server 2008 and later; x86 and x64, VC11-built
os_support.macos: no official php.net binary; source compile only
os_support.linux: no official php.net binary; source tarball only

added: use function / use const for namespace imports
limitations: OPcache still not enabled by default (7.0)

TLS negotiation regressed: default STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLS_CLIENT was widened to include TLS 1.1/1.2 in 5.6.0-5.6.6, then a compatibility fix in 5.6.7 reverted the default to TLS 1.0-only until PHP 7.2 restored a modern default -- code relying on 'default means TLS 1.2' on 5.6.7+ needed to pass explicit crypto-method flags
no scalar/return type declarations, no null coalescing operator (both 7.0)
last PHP 5 release; the 5.x object/array-copy-on-write engine is markedly slower than the phpng engine that shipped in 7.0

os_support.windows: Windows 7/Server 2008 R2 and later; x86 and x64, VC14-built (Visual Studio 2015); true 64-bit integers on Windows x64 for the first time
os_support.macos: no official php.net binary; source compile only
os_support.linux: no official php.net binary; source tarball only

added: the phpng engine rewrite: roughly 2x throughput and much lower memory use versus 5.6
scalar type declarations (int/float/string/bool, coercive and strict modes)
OPcache enabled and bundled by default
PHP 7 finally gives Windows x64 a real 64-bit zend_long, fixing the 32-bit-int-on-x64 limitation of 5.5/5.6
limitations: no strict_types enforcement unless the file opts in with declare(strict_types=1) -- coercive mode (silent int/string juggling) is still the default everywhere
no nullable types or void return type (7.1)
no object return type (7.2), no trailing commas in function calls (7.3)
no arrow functions, typed properties, or JIT (all land 7.4/8.0)
no Fibers -- async PHP still built on generators/callbacks (ReactPHP, Amp v1/v2) rather than true coroutines

os_support.windows: Windows 7/Server 2008 R2 and later; x86 and x64, VC14-built
os_support.macos: no official php.net binary; source compile only
os_support.linux: no official php.net binary; source tarball only

added: symmetric array unpacking with string keys deferred to 7.1's list() only for numeric
limitations: no object return type (7.2)
no arrow functions or typed properties (7.4)
no JIT (8.0)
TLS default still regressed to TLS-1.0-only for STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLS_CLIENT (fixed in 7.2)

os_support.windows: Windows 7/Server 2008 R2 and later (Windows Vista/Server 2008 support dropped with the move to VC15/Visual Studio 2017); x86 and x64
os_support.macos: no official php.net binary; source compile only
os_support.linux: no official php.net binary; source tarball only

added: TLS default crypto-method negotiation restored to include TLS 1.2 (rfc:improved-tls-defaults), after the 5.6.7-7.1.x regression to TLS-1.0-only
limitations: no arrow functions or typed properties (7.4)
no JIT (8.0)
no Fibers (8.1)
TLS 1.3 not available -- depends on OpenSSL 1.1.1, which ships with 7.4-era builds

os_support.windows: Windows 7/Server 2008 R2 and later; x86 and x64, VC15-built
os_support.macos: no official php.net binary; source compile only
os_support.linux: no official php.net binary; source tarball only

limitations: no arrow functions, typed properties, or bundled OpenSSL 1.1.1/TLS 1.3 (all 7.4)
no JIT (8.0), no Fibers (8.1)

os_support.windows: Windows 7/Server 2008 R2 and later; x86 and x64, VC15-built
os_support.macos: no official php.net binary; source compile only
os_support.linux: no official php.net binary; source tarball only

added: official Windows builds moved to a bundled OpenSSL 1.1.1 line, making TLS 1.3 usable via streams/curl for the first time
limitations: no JIT (8.0)
no union types, named arguments, or match expression (8.0)
no enums, readonly properties, or Fibers (8.1)
last PHP 7 release -- still using the pre-JIT Zend VM; CPU-bound workloads see no JIT speedup on this line

os_support.windows: Windows 7/Server 2008 R2 and later (Windows XP-era wording no longer applies; effectively 7+); x86 and x64, VS16-built (Visual Studio 2019)
os_support.macos: no official php.net binary; unofficial static-php-cli builds exist going back to this line
os_support.linux: no official php.net binary; unofficial static-php-cli builds exist going back to this line

added: JIT compiler (tracing and function JIT, opcache.jit)
limitations: JIT gives little to no benefit for typical I/O-bound web/CMS workloads (it mainly helps CPU-bound/numeric code) and shipped disabled by default

no enums, readonly properties, or Fibers (8.1) -- so no first-class coroutine primitive yet; ReactPHP/Amp/Swoole still rely on generators or Swoole's own coroutine runtime (a separate C extension) rather than a language-level primitive
no intersection types or 'never' return type (8.1)
this is the first major with any official Linux/macOS binaries in this catalog, and even those are the unofficial static-php-cli project, not php.net

os_support.windows: Windows 7/Server 2008 R2 and later (Microsoft's own VS2019 toolset still targets back to 7 SP1); x86 and x64, VS16-built
os_support.macos: no official php.net binary; static-php-cli unofficial builds available
os_support.linux: no official php.net binary; static-php-cli unofficial builds available

added: Fibers (language-level cooperative-concurrency primitive that ReactPHP/Amp v3 and Revolt build event loops on top of)
limitations: Fibers are cooperative, not preemptive -- a fiber that never yields still blocks the whole process; there is still no OS-thread-based true parallelism without ext-parallel/pthreads on a ZTS build, or a separate process model (Swoole, php-fpm workers)
no readonly promoted-constructor-property shorthand combined with all visibility combos until later patch/minor fixes
no enum interfaces' constants (8.2 refines), no readonly classes as a whole (8.2 is per-property only until 8.2's class-level readonly)
JIT still opt-in and still mostly irrelevant to typical web workloads

os_support.windows: Windows 7/Server 2008 R2 and later per Microsoft's VS2019/VS16 toolset floor; x86 and x64, VS16-built
os_support.macos: no official php.net binary; static-php-cli unofficial builds available
os_support.linux: no official php.net binary; static-php-cli unofficial builds available

added: standalone types (null, false, true as full types)
new in initializers extended to more positions
deprecation of dynamic properties (must opt in with #[AllowDynamicProperties])
limitations: no first-class support for 'never' unions beyond what 8.1 gave
no clone-with syntax (that is 8.5)
JIT and Fibers unchanged from 8.1 -- still opt-in JIT, still cooperative-only concurrency

os_support.windows: Windows 7/Server 2008 R2 and later per the VS16 (Visual Studio 2019) toolset this line still uses; x86 and x64
os_support.macos: no official php.net binary; static-php-cli unofficial builds available
os_support.linux: no official php.net binary; static-php-cli unofficial builds available

limitations: Windows 7/8 support was NOT dropped at this line -- that happens at 8.4 with the VS17 (Visual Studio 2022) toolset move; treat any claim that 8.3 drops Windows 7/8 as incorrect
no clone-with (8.5), no closures-in-const-expressions (8.5)

os_support.windows: minimum bumped to Windows 8/Server 2012 (Windows 7/Server 2008 R2 support dropped with the move to VS17/Visual Studio 2022, whose v143 toolset no longer targets Windows 7); x86 and x64
os_support.macos: no official php.net binary; static-php-cli unofficial builds available
os_support.linux: no official php.net binary; static-php-cli unofficial builds available

added: performance and memory improvements to the engine and standard library
limitations: this is the line where Windows 7 and Server 2008 R2 stop being supported -- a machine that could run 8.3 may not be able to run 8.4
property hooks add call overhead versus plain public properties -- not a free abstraction
JIT still opt-in; still limited benefit for typical web workloads

os_support.windows: Windows 8/Server 2012 and later per the VS17 (Visual Studio 2022) toolset; x86 and x64
os_support.macos: no official php.net binary; static-php-cli unofficial builds available
os_support.linux: no official php.net binary; static-php-cli unofficial builds available

added: clone with property updates (clone(...) with syntax)
limitations: still under a year old at research time (2026-09-17, released 2025-11-20) -- ecosystem/extension support (Swoole, Xdebug, etc.) for a fresh major typically lags by months
still no native async/await keyword or preemptive threading; Fibers plus userland event loops remain the concurrency model
JIT remains opt-in
